changes.comment: When "rush-client daemon status", "stop" or "restart" cannot reach a daemon whose process still runs, say what that process is doing and how to resume or stop it; "stop --force" also says that it killed no process. "rush-client daemon stop" now waits up to 15 s for a daemon that no longer listens to exit, instead of reporting that none runs while it still does. A command no longer runs Rush in-process beside this workspace's Rush daemon (on Linux, the process that the ownership record names, which has that record open) when its socket file was deleted; it fails with what that daemon is doing.
